speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of pancreatitis and current signs of obstructive jaundice, have you noticed any visible swelling of the gallbladder or felt a mass in your upper abdomen? I will also REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound to evaluate the biliary tree and pancreas.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasonography reveals an anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region. There is dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Serum studies show elevated Total Bilirubin (5.6 mg/dL), elevated Direct Bilirubin (4.8 mg/dL), and elevated Alkaline Phosphatase (192 U/L), while AST (32 U/L) and ALT (34 U/L) are within normal limits. Physical examination confirms a soft, cystic mass palpated in the right upper quadrant, consistent with the ultrasound findings.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless jaundice, weight loss, and palpable cystic gallbladder are classic signs of pancreatic cancer obstructing the bile duct. I will REQUEST IMAGES to visualize the mass and confirm the diagnosis.
